subject: Post-demo SLO runbook: proposed thresholds, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 12:15:00 -0700
Subject: BrightShore demo follow-up — perf targets & runbook draft

Vanessa / Lauren —

Great demo earlier today with Sam and Nora from BrightShore. They liked the streaming preview and how token-level latency looked on short responses, but asked for concrete acceptance criteria for a pilot. I put together a first-pass SLO runbook (attached) with thresholds we discussed on the call. High-level summary below: 

- Latency: p95 generation time <= 150ms for single-turn text responses (non-streaming)
- Streaming: chunk latency (first byte) <= 80ms, sustain rate >= 30 tokens/sec for long-running streams
- Throughput: 500 concurrent requests sustained across our Dedicated pool (expected burst to 800 for black swan)
- Concurrency: should support 50 concurrent open streaming sessions per customer region
- Availability target: 99.9% (monthly) for pilot workloads

Action items I captured:
1) Provide a short benchmark plan + sample payloads for BrightShore to run in their staging (we can run too) — owner: Vanessa
2) Confirm whether the p95 150ms target is acceptable as a signed pilot metric — owner: Sam/Nora
3) Identify fallback model variants (quantized, smaller context) for graceful degradation — owner: Soojin

Attaching the runbook draft and a short benchmarking checklist. Vanessa — can you surface any infra constraints (regions, GPU types) we should call out?

Thanks,
Ben

--
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightshore.com>, Nora Kim <nora.kim@brightshore.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightShore demo follow-up — perf targets & runbook draft

Sam / Nora —

Thanks again for the time today. Attaching the SLO runbook and a brief benchmarking instructions file (small payloads + longer streaming scenarios). A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

- The p95 <= 150ms for single-turn non-streaming is achievable on our Dedicated configurations using A100-class instances with our continuous batching profile tuned to small payloads. If you expect larger context windows (1k+ tokens), that p95 is likely to rise — we call that out in the attached sheet.

- For streaming, our suggested acceptance bands are: first-byte latency <= 80ms and sustained token emit rate >= 25-35 tokens/sec (we used 30 tokens/sec as a target in the runbook). We also recommend p99 monitoring on chunk latency for pilot safety.

- Throughput / concurrency: 500 sustained RPS (concurrent requests) is a good starting point. We'll provision a Dedicated pool sized for that, with a documented burst plan up to ~800. Note that for streaming-heavy workloads the memory (KV cache) usage grows — team will size cache accordingly.

Next steps proposed: 
1) BrightShore to confirm target p95 and streaming acceptance bands by EOD Mon 04/05 — Sam/Nora
2) We schedule a 2-hour benchmark window (mutually agreed) where BrightShore runs their staging workload and we run the same traffic from our side (results joined) — owner: Vanessa + BrightShore infra; suggested dates: 04/07 or 04/08
3) If benchmarks meet thresholds, we issue pilot access (30-day pilot) and collect week-1 telemetry for a formal SLO sign-off — owner: Ben + CS

I'm copying Soojin who will own fallback/variant model configs and Lauren for procurement checklist (if pilot needs a PO).

Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (212) 555-0123

Attachments: slo-runbook-proposal.xlsx, benchmark-instructions.md

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@brightshore.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nora Kim <nora.kim@brightshore.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: BrightShore demo follow-up — perf targets & runbook draft

Thanks Vanessa — this is helpful. A couple quick notes from BrightShore infra/engineering: 

- The p95 <= 150ms for typical shorter responses is acceptable as our initial acceptance bar. We will flag longer context use cases separately.
- Streaming: first byte <= 80ms is tight but reasonable for the regional cloud near us; sustained 30 tokens/sec target also seems fine. We will run a subset of our production traces in staging during the benchmark window.
- Throughput: 500 sustained concurrent requests aligns with our peak planning, but we need the burst behavior documented for our risk committee.

We can commit to confirming formally by EOD 2027-04-05. For the benchmark window, 04/07 10:00–12:00 PT works for our infra team. Please send any ip ranges or auth tokens we should use. Also can you confirm which model variant you plan to use for the pilot (baseline + fallback)?

Sam

Sam Patel
Sr. Engineering Manager, Platform
BrightShore Health
sam.patel@brightshore.com | +1 (650) 555-3344

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Benchmark ops and procurement notes (BrightShore)

Team —

Quick internal checklist after Sam's sign-off: 

- Confirm pilot model set: baseline = rdx-base-1.3 (int8 quant) ; fallback = rdx-small-0.9 (lower mem/latency) — owner: Soojin to confirm exact quantization profile and kernel choices.
- Infra: reserve Dedicated pool in us-east-1 with 8x A100-80GB initially (fits 500 sustained streams in our perf model). Add autoscale buffer of 2 nodes for observed bursts. — owner: Vanessa + Infra ops
- IP allowlist & tokens: generate staging service account token and share secure link to BrightShore (use Drive link above). — owner: Lauren
- Procurement: Lauren to send pilot SOW + PO template; allow for 30-day pilot billing and an SLA uplift if they opt into 99.95 later. 
- Benchmark window: confirm 04/07 10:00–12:00 PT and circulate traffic generator payloads (attached file).

I'll update the runbook with the node sizing assumptions and quant profiles before the benchmark. If anyone sees a different sizing recommendation, flag it here.

Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
